ORDER This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.66/2023 dated 29.03.2023 registered at Police Station Ghughri, District Mandla (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 366, 376,
376(2)(1), 376(D) of IPC and Section 92 of Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

He further submits that when applicant and prosecutrix have filed an application for marriage before the competent authority, a false case was registered against the applicant; that there is a delay in lodging the FIR.
He also submits that the applicant is 24 years young youth, who he is in custody since 04.05.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.

He further submits that the applicant is a permanent resident of the district and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence; that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be Atul Jhariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123907646/
1 imposed by this Court.

sentences.text: On these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Applicant has prayed for bail on the ground that this Court vide order dated 09.05.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.17028/2023 has granted bail to the co- accused persons who are the parents of present applicant, but they have been given the benefit of bail in absence of any evidence regarding their direct involvement in commission of crime.
Applicant is the main accused of the crime, who allegedly promised to marry a physically challenged prosecutrix and sexually abused her.

Though the application for marriage submitted before the Special Marriage Officer, affidavits in support of that application, order passed by the special marriage officer etc. have been filed as Annexure A-2, but these documents merely disclose that the applicant moved an application for marriage before the Court, but he never solemnized the marriage.

The notice issued by the Special Marriage Officer disclose that the due date fixed for filing the objection was 27.03.2023 and the FIR was made on 29.03.2023; apparently applicant failed to solemnize the marriage in between that period.
In the light of these facts, the grounds pleaded by the applicant for seeking bail cannot be the basis to allow this application.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. is dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE rv Atul Jhariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123907646/
